review_type: Targeted documentation review for the narrative and architecture revision
boundary: This record identifies claims actually checked in official documentation. It is not an exhaustive audit of every retained statement or a live service test. Diagrams are authored logical explanations, and use-case narratives are proposed engineering workflows.

claims_checked: Named built-in observability, source-control, and incident-coordination providers
Two-way telemetry, one-way reads, and bring-your-own integration paths are distinct
Webhook initiation does not itself provide telemetry-read authorization
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: The inventory separates evidence sources, incident initiation, tool invocation, and lifecycle delivery instead of assigning identical behavior to every connector.

claims_checked: Azure Resources and Azure DevOps registrations have separate purposes
Subscription and project association differ
Externally hosted repository contents are not automatically supplied by pipeline access
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: Azure infrastructure and delivery context are separate rows and configuration explanations.

claims_checked: Trigger-created custom-agent schedules use a flexible window of up to 30 minutes
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: Renamed the minute-by-minute report to Incident status bulletin. The guide distinguishes telemetry resolution, lookback window, scheduled start, and execution duration. No exact-minute delivery guarantee is made.

claims_checked: Store descriptions and entry descriptions precede selected full-content reads
Memory is versioned informational context, distinct from skill procedures and standing instructions
Monitor history and corrective reflections have separate production paths
Environment understanding, dependency, pipeline, and tool-use knowledge are represented as managed memory
Different managed stores have different refresh triggers and retention behavior
A store is not a same-investigation cache for raw tool output
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: Explained production, retention, retrieval, correction, and access separately. Refresh thresholds vary across retrieved documentation versions; the environment-refresh section describes the conditions and links the current official thresholds rather than freezing a conflicting interval. No undocumented backup, universal vector index, or model-weight training mechanism is asserted.

claims_checked: A new custom agent requires explicit memory-store attachments
Managed and custom store write behavior differs
Agent definition and individual invocation are separate objects
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: The explanations distinguish contextual availability from retrieval and execution. Shared handoffs preserve product-specific identifiers rather than claim a common runtime.

claims_checked: Account-level integration registration precedes Agent Space resource selection
Supported GitHub, GitLab, Bitbucket Cloud, and Confluence Cloud variants
Read context and optional repository write features have separate settings
The documented repository write actions exclude public repositories
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: Provider editions, selected resources, and permitted effects are shown explicitly. No unsupported self-hosted Bitbucket claim was added.

claims_checked: Same-account S3 sources and assessment-specific source-format requirements
Selected Confluence pages provide documentation context
Source registration, resource selection, and assessment configuration are distinct steps
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: Documentation context is not described as a source-code repository or a universal persistent incident-memory system.

claims_checked: Jira Cloud application authorization and site registration
Project-specific issue-creation and comment permissions
Disconnecting does not delete existing external issues
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: The publication path and its retained external records are explained separately from assessment execution.

claims_checked: Application sources, scope, and assessment criteria serve different roles
Assessment configurations and runs have feature-specific lifecycles
Findings are execution evidence rather than a documented universal vulnerability-memory store
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: Added an application-context chapter and logical data-flow diagram. The cross-product handoff schema remains explicitly team-authored, not an AWS API.

claims_checked: Credential retrieval and application authentication are different stages
Login Optimization retains and reuses a successful login procedure
Disabling reuse does not establish deletion of the learned procedure
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: The authentication workflow distinguishes source access, login navigation, actual role, and protected-route coverage.

claims_checked: Cost, anomaly, recommendation, and operational-change services supply different evidence
Recommendation provenance belongs to the documented upstream services
Agent data permissions and operator access have separate roles
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: The data-source inventory does not import DevOps Agent MCP support or imply independent computation of optimization recommendations.

claims_checked: Uploaded files are operator-maintained and read-only to the agent
Preferences and corrections can persist across sessions
Older conversation content is summarized separately from persistent memory
Persistent instance-local context and isolated ephemeral runtime have different lifecycles
Soft deletion, memory correction, task cancellation, and whole-agent deletion are object-specific controls
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: The guide distinguishes retrieval from restoration, file updates from memory changes, and persistent state from the runtime. No universal backup or cross-instance shared-memory mechanism is asserted.

claims_checked: Provider registration and agent-specific destination binding differ
Jira supports the documented read, issue, and comment operations rather than arbitrary workflow management
Slack is a one-way publication path in the reviewed preview
Jira approval differs by invocation path, and Slack posting has no per-action prompt
reviewed_claim_groups.editorial_result: The catalog narratives and integration diagrams preserve destination-specific effect boundaries.

retained_material: Other detailed procedures retain the previous edition's official references and source-version qualifications. They were not all re-executed or exhaustively re-audited in this revision.

catalog_consolidation.scope: Classification, relationships and implementation recipes. No exhaustive re-audit of retained guide prose.
catalog_consolidation.qualification: Retrieved DevOps overview/creation versions do not enumerate every attachment detail retained in the existing guide. No absence was interpreted as removal. CronSchedule and Security revalidation could not be newly fetched; their existing references remain qualified rather than marked freshly verified.
catalog_consolidation.additional_check: Built-in on-demand queries versus user-defined custom reporting were reconfirmed from the Custom Agents overview. FinOps invocation-dependent publication and the Security configuration/run lifecycle were also rechecked. Source absence was not interpreted as feature removal.
